comparison: Both evaluate hetero-aggregate and homo-aggregate formation (C48-C52). OpenEval finds the co-immunoprecipitation and microscopy data sufficient to demonstrate spatial segregation. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about protein expression levels, requesting Western blots to confirm the actual protein ratios, which affects confidence in the segregation mechanism.

Both address collagen transport through stapled Golgi (C42-C44). OpenEval finds the quantitative transport kinetics convincing. Peer reviewers question whether the measured collagen secretion represents newly synthesized versus previously secreted collagen, and request half-life comparisons to rule out transient traffic blocks in 'dead' Golgi.

Both evaluate VSV-G transport experiments (C39-C41). OpenEval considers the functional validation strong. Peer reviewers express concern about co-transfection efficiency, questioning whether VSV-G transport was measured in cells actually containing stapled Golgi or in non-transfected cells within the population.

Both address BFA treatment and FRAP analysis (C45-C47). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these control experiments demonstrate that staples do not grossly disrupt Golgi structure or enzyme dynamics, with no concerns raised by reviewers.

Both evaluate evidence for cis-Golgi staple localization and immobility (C27-C29, C31-C32, C35-C36). OpenEval finds the convergence of imaging and biochemical data convincing. Peer reviewers note heterogeneity, suggesting 'some staples may be in cis and others trans,' creating uncertainty about whether all staples truly remain static at cis-Golgi.

Both address temperature block experiments and cis-Golgi retention (C22-C25). OpenEval finds the reversibility controls and glycan analysis convincing. Peer reviewers' concern about staple heterogeneity and potential 'dead' Golgi effects extends to these localization claims, creating uncertainty.

Both evaluate the basic staple formation and characterization (C1, C13-C15). OpenEval finds the electron microscopy evidence and cytosolic control convincing. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the staple system itself, focusing concerns on downstream experimental interpretations rather than the fundamental tool.

Both address disaggregated CD8lumenal behavior as secretory cargo (C16-C20). OpenEval finds the complementary biochemical and imaging approaches convincing. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about the controllability and reversibility of the staple system, suggesting acceptance.

Both evaluate electron microscopy observations of spatial distribution (C30, C37-C38). OpenEval finds the structural observations and mechanistic inference reasonable. Peer reviewers did not challenge these EM findings about localization patterns, suggesting implicit acceptance.

Both address differential fates of soluble versus membrane aggregates (C53-C55). OpenEval finds the quantitative EM data and secretion assays convincing. Peer reviewers' concerns about protein expression levels (requesting Western blots) create uncertainty about whether observed differences reflect the proposed mechanism or protein abundance.

Both address spatial segregation observations (C3, C57). OpenEval finds the differential localization of soluble versus membrane aggregates well-supported. Peer reviewers did not challenge the basic structural observations, suggesting acceptance of the spatial patterns.

Both evaluate spatial segregation and mechanistic explanations (C4, C58-C59). OpenEval finds the structural inferences logical. Peer reviewers accepted the EM observations showing localization patterns without challenge.

Both address the rim progression model (C5, C60). OpenEval finds the model well-supported by differential behavior observations. Peer reviewers' concerns about experimental design (co-transfection, protein levels, collagen experiments) and statement that 'there is no known cargo of this type' create uncertainty about generalizing to normal Golgi transport.

Both evaluate the two-domain functional model (C72-C73). OpenEval finds the synthesis of spatial segregation and differential mobility convincing. Peer reviewers' concerns about the artificiality of the staple system and request to 'clearly state' there is 'no known cargo of this type' suggest uncertainty about the model's general applicability.

Both address cisternal immobility across the Golgi stack (C33-C34). OpenEval finds the extension from cis-Golgi to entire stack convincing. Peer reviewers' note about staple heterogeneity ('some staples may be in cis and others trans') creates uncertainty about whether immobility applies uniformly.

Both address implications for cisternal maturation (C68). OpenEval finds the claims appropriately cautious but notes speculation. Peer reviewers' concerns about experimental limitations and artificiality of the system align with uncertainty about broader conclusions regarding maturation mechanisms.

Both evaluate the proposed transport mechanism for large aggregates (C69). OpenEval finds the rim progression proposal well-supported by experimental data. Peer reviewers' concerns about the artificiality of staples and lack of natural cargo analogs create uncertainty about this mechanism's physiological relevance.

OpenEval evaluates reinterpretation of published collagen data (C61-C62). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer concerns about collagen experiments (R1) may indirectly relate to interpretation of prior literature.
OpenEval finds speculative claims about fission/fusion mechanisms (C63-C65) uncertain due to lack of direct experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates background literature and context (C6-C12, C67) as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on experimental claims rather than literature review.
